title: Routing: per-(model, region, tier) circuit breaker state store + evaluation API
creator: Mina Haddad
body:
Goal
Introduce a routing-owned circuit breaker state store keyed by (model, region, tier) and a lightweight evaluation API that the gateway/control-plane can call to deterministically decide: allow vs shed vs degrade (fallback hint), without relying on implicit timeouts.

This is the foundational primitive for layered overload protection:
- Gateway admission control can ask routing for breaker state + recommended action.
- Routing can incorporate capacity signals + runtime backpressure hints to transition breaker states.
- Runtime can still shed locally, but routing-level breaker prevents cascading queue blowups by shedding earlier.

References
- ADR-0148: Circuit breaker state model and hysteresis (closed/open/half-open, cooldowns, transition rules)
- ADR-0147: Overload error taxonomy and HTTP mapping (routing returns structured reason/action; gateway maps to 429/503 + Redwood error codes)
- Initiative umbrella: ENG-4821

Scope
1) State store
- Key: (model_id, region, tier)
  - model_id should align with routing’s canonical model identifier (pinned version where applicable, but breaker should generally operate at the serving target level; see Open Questions).
  - tier aligns with existing customer tiering used by routing policies (e.g., free/pro/enterprise/internal).
- State: CLOSED | OPEN | HALF_OPEN
- Metadata:
  - opened_at, last_transition_at
  - open_reason (enum) and primary_signal (enum) for debugging/telemetry
  - counters used for half-open probe logic (successes/failures window)
  - cooldown_until / next_allowed_probe_at
  - optional “shed_hint” describing preferred shed mode (edge shed vs runtime shed) and recommended Retry-After seconds

2) Evaluation API
- Provide an internal API from routing service:
  - EvaluateBreaker(model_id, region, tier, request_class)
  - Response: decision=ALLOW|SHED|DEGRADE, breaker_state, reason, retry_after_seconds (optional), fallback_allowed (bool), fallback_targets (optional, bounded)
- This ticket focuses on the API contract and routing-side evaluation. Gateway integration is handled in ENG-4822.
- Request classification inputs should be minimal to avoid high cardinality. Proposed request_class fields:
  - is_streaming (bool)
  - route_family (chat/completions/embeddings) OR a bounded route enum
  - optional “latency_sensitive” (bool) if already available from tier/policy

3) Persistence & consistency
- Store should be fast, highly available, and safe under routing deploys.
- Proposed implementation (v1): in-memory state machine + shared Redis (or equivalent) backing for cross-instance coordination.
  - State updates use compare-and-set semantics on version/etag to avoid split-brain.
  - TTL: state entries should not disappear during prolonged overload; use long TTL (e.g., 24h) with periodic refresh, or no TTL with explicit cleanup when a model/region/tier is retired.
- Must tolerate partial failures of the store:
  - If store unavailable: fail “closed” from a platform stability perspective (i.e., default to SHED for the affected key) OR “allow” with guardrails? Decision: default SHED when store is unreachable for >N ms to prevent cascading failures; log as internal error and emit metric. (Confirm with SRE; see Open Questions.)

Functional requirements
- Correct implementation of ADR-0148 state transitions:
  - OPEN when signal breaches threshold for X seconds (hysteresis)
  - CLOSED when signal below close threshold for Y seconds
  - HALF_OPEN after cooldown; allow limited probes; re-open on probe failures
- Hysteresis parameters must be configurable per model/region/tier with safe defaults.
- Idempotent & monotonic transitions (no rapid flapping under jittery signals).
- Bounded decision latency: p99 EvaluateBreaker < 5ms within region.

Non-functional requirements
- Telemetry:
  - breaker_state gauge per (model, region, tier)
  - transitions counter with from_state/to_state + reason
  - evaluate calls counter + decision counts
  - store read/write latency + error rates
  - “store_unavailable_fallback_mode” counter
- Cardinality constraints:
  - limit label values; do not include customer_id, request_id, or raw route strings
- Safety:
  - guardrails to prevent opening breakers globally due to a single bad model_id input; validate model_id/region/tier against routing catalog.

Deliverables
- Routing service implementation of breaker state machine + store adapter
- Public internal interface (proto / REST) for evaluation
- Unit tests for transitions & probe logic
- Minimal load test to validate store behavior under concurrent evaluators
- Docs (internal) describing API contract + failure modes + operational overrides

Acceptance criteria
- Breaker state is shared across routing instances and survives deploy/rollout.
- Evaluation API returns deterministic decision + reason, used by gateway to map to ADR-0147 errors (integration tested via mocked gateway caller).
- Half-open probe behavior is bounded (no thundering herd) and configurable.
- Basic dashboards can show breaker state over time (metrics emitted with agreed names/labels).

Open questions
1) Keying by model version vs model family
- For v1: key by routing “serving target” (model_id includes major serving config) to avoid one variant poisoning others, but avoid exploding keys with every patch version. Proposal: key by model family + quantization/profile class (e.g., llama3.1-70b + fp16/int8) rather than exact build id.

2) Default behavior when store is unavailable
- Proposal above: default SHED after a small timeout to protect system stability; add an allowlist for internal tiers to fail-open if needed for debugging.

3) Fallback hints
- This ticket includes optional fields for future fallback/degrade decisions, but we should keep payload stable and bounded. Routing should return at most 2 fallback targets.

Implementation notes
- Use the same breaker logic library intended for gateway/routing/runtime where possible, but keep ownership in routing.
- Persist a compact struct; avoid storing high-frequency counters as separate keys.
- Add an admin-only override hook (read-only in v1; write/override tracked separately). Emergency toggle request tracked in INT-1182.

Progress / updates
- 2025-11-06 (Ravi): Drafted proto for EvaluateBreaker + response shape. Sync’d with Brian Murphy on ADR-0147 mapping: routing returns reason/action only; gateway owns HTTP status and body mapping.
- 2025-11-14 (Ravi): Implemented state machine per ADR-0148 behind feature flag "routing.breakers.enabled". Added basic transition tests incl. cooldown + half-open probes.
- 2025-11-20 (Christine): Reviewed hysteresis defaults; flagged risk of flapping if signal window < 30s. Suggested separate open/close thresholds and minimum dwell time in state.
- 2025-12-02 (Ravi): Added Redis-backed store with CAS on version. Implemented fallback behavior when store read fails (default SHED for non-internal tiers, ALLOW for internal tier). Added metrics for store errors.
- 2025-12-09 (Mina): API contract reviewed with gateway + runtime teams. Agreed that EvaluateBreaker call must be optional; gateway will treat routing timeout as SHED with overload reason "routing_unavailable".
- 2026-01-08 (Ravi): Landed in routing service; integrated with feature-flag config plumbing. Follow-up tracked in ENG-4825 to wire capacity signals into open/close decisions.

Links
- Related PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18457 (Routing service circuit breaker state machine implementation with hysteresis and persistence)
- Initiative: ENG-4821
- Next: ENG-4825 (capacity signals integration)

Follow-ups
- Add explicit rate limiting on half-open probes per key (if needed based on canary).
- Confirm final keying strategy once model catalog naming scheme is finalized for Hosted vs Dedicated alignment (ENG-4837).
